Requires agencies receiving reports to enter the firearm's information into the national crime information center database.

bills.title: Concerning the use of deadly physical force against a person who has made an illegal entry into a place of business.
bills.summary: Extends the existing right to use deadly physical force against an intruder, under certain conditions, to additional actors. Covers owners of a business facing an illegal entry. Also covers the business's managers and employees.

bills.title: Concerning the need for services for juveniles with severe behavioral health conditions in the context of school safety, including residential treatment.
bills.summary: Directs the school safety resource center to convene a working group of stakeholders to assess school districts' needs regarding residential mental health treatment for children and youth identified by school personnel as having severe behavioral or mental health disorders. Has the working group gather information on the availability, need, and cost of residential treatment services for children and youth in Colorado. Requires the center to use the data to prepare a report with legislative recommendations addressing those mental health needs. Requires presentation of the report and recommendations at its January 2021 committee-of-reference hearing under the SMART Government Act.

bills.title: Concerning creating a multi-agency working group to address school safety.
bills.summary: Creates the Colorado interagency working group on school safety, a 14-member body whose mission is enhancing school safety through cost-effective use of public resources. Assigns it to study and implement the September 2019 state auditor's school safety recommendations, consider program reorganization, identify shared effectiveness metrics, and improve interagency coordination and communication. Tasks it with increasing transparency and accessibility of state grants, including common applications and outreach for districts without grant writers, and with facilitating legally allowable data sharing. Lets the group contract for a consultant, funded by appropriations or gifts, though it meets only when the department of public safety identifies sufficient funding.
sponsors: Gardner Gonzales, Fields, Lundeen, Jenet, Van Winkle, Beckman, Sirota

bills.title: Concerning school safety plans for all schools in each school district.
bills.summary: Directs each district school board to issue a request for proposals for a district-wide school safety assessment. Requires the district to contract a school safety expert to evaluate every public school in the district and report recommendations to the board, which must vote on each one. Requires the board to present approved recommendations to the state board of education, which votes on them and provides funding for the approved items. Requires the state board to report to the legislature's education committees on the recommendations it receives, approves, and funds.

bills.title: Concerning the creation of the law enforcement, public safety, and criminal justice information sharing grant program, and, in connection therewith, making an appropriation.
bills.summary: Creates the law enforcement, public safety, and criminal justice information sharing grant program within the division of homeland security and emergency management to help local law enforcement agencies access the Colorado information sharing consortium's system. Allows grant money to pay for computer hardware, software, and programming needed to connect to those systems. Conditions grants on compliance with federal data security requirements and federal rules governing criminal justice information systems. Creates the program fund, repeals the program on July 1, 2022, and appropriates $500,000 from the marijuana tax cash fund for implementation.
sponsors: Rep. Adrienne Benavidez, Sen. Rhonda Fields

bills.title: “Red Flag” Gun Confiscation
bills.summary: Creates a process, beginning January 1, 2020, for a family or household member or a law enforcement officer to petition a court for a temporary extreme risk protection order. Requires the petitioner to establish by a preponderance of the evidence that a person poses a significant risk to self or others by having a firearm in their custody or control or by possessing, purchasing, or receiving one, supported by a sworn affidavit setting forth the supporting facts. Requires the court to hold the temporary hearing in person or by telephone on the day the petition is filed or the next court day, followed by a second hearing within 14 days to determine whether a continuing order is warranted. Provides for court-appointed counsel to represent the respondent at the hearings.

bills.title: Concerning expanded disclosure about electioneering communications.
bills.summary: The state constitution defines electioneering communications as those referring unambiguously to a candidate within 30 days before a primary or 60 days before a general election. Expands the statutory definition for campaign finance disclosure to also capture qualifying communications disseminated between the primary and general elections. Requires any person spending $1,000 or more per calendar year on electioneering communications to state their name in the communication, following the existing requirements for independent expenditures.
sponsors: Sen. Rachel Zenzinger, Sen. Jack Tate, Rep. Mike Weissman

bills.title: Concerning firearm possession by persons who lawfully use medical marijuana.
bills.summary: Clarifies that a prior conviction for possessing or using marijuana lawfully under the Colorado constitution does not prohibit a person from carrying a firearm. Clarifies that lawful medical marijuana use does not make a person ineligible to possess firearms under federal law or an unlawful user of a controlled substance for concealed handgun permit purposes. Prohibits the department of public safety from sharing confidential medical marijuana registry information with law enforcement for firearm-transfer background checks. Leaves the existing prohibitions tied to other felony convictions intact.
sponsors: Sen. Vicki Marble, Rep. Bri Buentello

bills.title: Concerning the repeal of certain provisions concerning ammunition magazines.
bills.summary: Repeals the statutory prohibition on possessing certain ammunition magazines. Also strikes the requirement that covered magazines manufactured in Colorado on or after July 1, 2013 carry a permanent stamp or marking showing that manufacture date. Eliminates both provisions from the statute books.

bills.title: Concerning fines assessed for violations of laws administered by the division of parks and wildlife.
bills.summary: Changes the fine amounts for violations of laws enforced by the division of parks and wildlife. Restructures how collected fines are distributed: when a parks and wildlife officer issues the citation, all of the fine now goes to the relevant division fund, rather than half to the general fund. When another Colorado peace officer issues the citation, half goes to the relevant division fund and half to the issuing local government or state agency. Applies these disposition changes across the affected fine provisions.
sponsors: Rep. Marc Catlin, Sen. Don Coram

bills.title: Concerning allowing concealed handgun permit holders to carry concealed handguns on school grounds.
bills.summary: Current law, with exceptions, restricts concealed handgun permit holders by barring carry on public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school grounds. Removes that restriction. Keeps the existing exceptions to the school-grounds prohibition unchanged.

bills.title: Concerning the use of deadly physical force against a person who has made an illegal entry into a place of business.
bills.summary: Extends the existing right to use deadly physical force against an unlawful intruder, under certain conditions, to additional actors. Adds owners of a place of business. Also adds the managers and employees of the business.

bills.title: Concerning crimes related to multi-burst trigger activators, and, in connection therewith, making an appropriation.
bills.summary: Expands the definition of dangerous weapon to include a multi-burst trigger activator, defined as a device attached to a semiautomatic firearm that lets it discharge two or more shots in a burst, or a manual or power-driven trigger-activating device that increases the firearm's rate of fire. Subjects possession of such a device to the existing dangerous-weapon penalties, a class 5 felony for a first offense and a class 4 felony for each subsequent one. Makes selling a multi-burst trigger activator to another person, or purchasing one from another person, a class 5 felony. Raises repeat purchase-and-sale violations to a class 4 felony.

bills.title: Concerning the repeal of certain provisions concerning ammunition magazines.
bills.summary: Repeals the statutory prohibition on possessing certain ammunition magazines. Also repeals the requirement that covered magazines manufactured in Colorado on or after July 1, 2013 carry a permanent stamp or marking showing they were made or assembled after that date. Strikes both provisions from state law.
sponsors: Sen. Hill, Rep. Saine, Rep. Humphrey

bills.title: Concerning allowing a law-abiding person to carry a concealed handgun without a permit, and, in connection therewith, preserving current laws restricting the carrying of concealed handguns on certain property including public schools and reducing an appropriation.
bills.summary: Allows a person who legally possesses a handgun under state and federal law to carry it concealed in Colorado without a permit. Gives a person carrying under that authority the same rights and the same limitations that apply to permit holders. Preserves the existing prohibitions on concealed carry in places such as public elementary, middle, junior high, and high school grounds, and reduces an appropriation.

bills.title: Concerning the use of deadly physical force against a person who has made an illegal entry into a place of business.
bills.summary: Extends the existing right to use deadly physical force against an intruder, under certain conditions, to additional protected actors. Adds owners of a business. Also adds the managers and employees of the business.

bills.title: Concerning the repeal of certain provisions concerning ammunition magazines.
bills.summary: Repeals the statutory provisions prohibiting possession of certain ammunition magazines. Also eliminates the requirement that covered magazines made in Colorado on or after July 1, 2013 be permanently stamped or marked to show that manufacture date. Removes both provisions from the statutes.
sponsors: Rep. Humphrey, Rep. Saine, Sen. Hill

bills.summary: Current law, with exceptions, bars concealed handgun permit holders from carrying on public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school grounds. Removes that limitation on permit holders. Leaves the existing exceptions to the school-grounds prohibition untouched.

bills.title: Concerning the use of deadly physical force against a person who has made an illegal entry into a place of business.
bills.summary: Extends the existing right to use deadly physical force against an unlawful intruder, under certain conditions, to more actors. Covers owners of a business. Also covers the managers and employees of the business.

bills.title: Concerning a restriction on a state agency's authority to increase a fee.
bills.summary: Requires every state agency fee increase, beginning September 1, 2018, to take effect on July 1 of a year, with an exception for emergency increases. Bars an agency from raising a fee unless it submits a proposal with specified information to the joint budget committee by the preceding February 1, a majority of the committee approves it without alteration, and authorizing legislation granting the increase is enacted. Lets agencies adopt emergency fee increases outside that process. Requires an agency adopting an emergency increase to submit the proposal to the committee by the next February 1.

bills.title: Concerning the issuance of capitol identification cards to members of the public to permit them entry to state buildings containing the legislative branch of state government without having to submit to personal security checks.
bills.summary: Authorizes capitol security personnel, including the Colorado state patrol, to let holders of a state capitol ID card enter the capitol, state services, and legislative services buildings without a search of their person or property or weapons screening. Directs the secretary of the senate or the chief clerk of the house to issue the credential to any applicant who pays a fee and completes a fingerprint-based criminal history record check. Issues each credential for a 2-year period. Sets the initial fee at $100, with the amount set to cover the actual costs of administering the program.
sponsors: Sen. Cooke, Rep. Van Winkle, Rep. Williams

bills.title: Concerning the nonsubstantive relocation of laws from title 12, Colorado Revised Statutes, as part of the organizational recodification of title 12.
bills.summary: Implements the initial recommendations of the recodification study of title 12, which covers professions and occupations. Relocates the Colorado Parental Notification Act to a new part of title 13 and the firearms dealer laws to a new part of title 18. Moves the gun show background check laws to title 18 as well, along with the Uniform Unsworn Declarations Act to title 13. Makes conforming amendments and repeals the provisions at their former locations.
sponsors: Sen. Cooke, Sen. Gardner, Rep. Herod, Rep. Foote

bills.title: Concerning the penalty for a person who commits burglary to acquire firearms, and, in connection therewith, making an appropriation.
bills.summary: Designates a third type of second-degree burglary as a class 3 felony, joining the two circumstances already elevated above the class 4 baseline. Covers burglary whose objective is the theft of one or more firearms or ammunition. Authorizes a fine of at least $5,000 and up to $750,000 in addition to any other sentence upon conviction. Makes the required 5-year statutory appropriation.

bills.title: Concerning creation of an extreme risk protection order.
bills.summary: Creates a process for a family or household member or a law enforcement officer to petition a court for a temporary extreme risk protection order. Requires the petitioner to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the person poses a significant risk to self or others by having a firearm in their custody or control or by acquiring one, backed by a sworn affidavit stating the supporting facts. Requires the temporary hearing in person or by telephone on the filing day or the next court day. Requires a second hearing within 7 days of the temporary order to decide whether a continuing order is warranted.
sponsors: Rep. Alec Garnett and Rep. Cole Wist

bills.title: Concerning handgun safety training courses for school employees, and, in connection therewith, permitting certain school employees to carry concealed handguns in public schools.
bills.summary: Allows a county sheriff to provide a handgun safety training course to employees of public elementary, middle, junior high, or high schools who hold concealed handgun permits. Requires the sheriff to consult with each school district board of education, and the state charter school institute where applicable, in setting the curriculum. Requires the curriculum to account for existing emergency response frameworks and to satisfy insurability standards for armed school employees.

bills.title: Concerning allowing certain military personnel who are less than twenty-one years of age to obtain a permit to carry a concealed handgun.
bills.summary: Existing law requires a concealed handgun permit applicant to be at least 21 years old. Amends the age requirement to accept applicants who are 18 or older and on active duty in, or honorably discharged from, any branch or reserve branch of the United States military, including the National Guard. Leaves the 21-year minimum in place for all other applicants.

bills.title: Concerning the repeal of certain provisions concerning ammunition magazines.

sponsors: Sen. Marble, Rep. Humphrey, Rep. Saine

bills.title: Concerning legalizing certain knives.
bills.summary: Removes gravity knives and switchblade knives from the statutory definition of illegal weapon. Legalizes possession of those knives as a result. Leaves other categories of illegal weapons untouched.

bills.title: Concerning permitting the carrying of concealed handguns on public school grounds.
bills.summary: Current law, with exceptions, restricts concealed handgun permit holders by prohibiting carry on public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school grounds. Removes that restriction. Keeps the existing exceptions to the school-grounds prohibition unchanged.

bills.summary: Creates a new exemption to the offense of unlawfully carrying a concealed weapon. Applies the exemption when the person is on active duty serving in the armed forces of the United States military. Limits the exemption to cases where the weapon is a concealed handgun.

bills.summary: Current law, with exceptions, limits concealed handgun permit holders by barring carry on the grounds of public elementary, middle, junior high, and high schools. Removes that limitation for permit holders. Preserves the existing exceptions to the school-grounds prohibition.

bills.summary: Repeals the state restrictions on large-capacity ammunition magazines. Eliminates the associated requirements imposed on such magazines under those provisions. Strikes the provisions from state law.
sponsors: Sen. Marble, Rep. Saine & Rep. Humphrey

bills.title: Concerning allowing certain military personnel who are less than twenty-one years of age to obtain a permit to carry a concealed handgun.
bills.summary: Opens concealed handgun permits to military personnel who are younger than 21. Applies to members of the military who would otherwise satisfy the permit criteria. Leaves the 21-year age requirement in place for non-military applicants.

bills.title: Concerning the governor's authority to restrict the distribution of firearms during a state of disaster emergency.
bills.summary: Addresses the governor's authority over firearms during a state of disaster emergency. Removes the authority to restrict the distribution of firearms during such an emergency. Leaves other disaster-emergency powers unaffected.

bills.title: Concerning an exception to the prohibition against disclosing confidential communications with a mental health professional when school safety is at risk.
bills.summary: Current law generally bars mental health professionals from disclosing confidential client communications without consent. Creates an exception when the client makes an articulable and significant threat against a school or its occupants. Also creates an exception when the client exhibits behavior that, in the professional's reasonable judgment, creates an articulable and significant threat to students, teachers, administrators, or other school personnel. Limits any such disclosure to appropriate school or district personnel and law enforcement agencies, with the information otherwise kept confidential.

bills.title: Concerning protecting animal species threatened with extinction by prohibiting trafficking.
bills.summary: Prohibits the sale, purchase, trade, or distribution of parts and products of covered animal species, with limited exceptions. Excludes guns, knives, and musical instruments from the prohibition. Establishes an unclassified misdemeanor for a first offense and an unclassified felony for second and subsequent offenses, each with monetary penalties. Authorizes Colorado wildlife officers and other commissioned officers of the wildlife division to enforce the provisions.
